properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 1:52AM EDT until September 22 at 4:45AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northeastern Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 152 AM EDT, gauge reports indicated heavy rain due to
Flooding. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Marietta.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Knox, KY
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 22 at 1:46AM EDT until September 22 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Knox County in southeastern Kentucky...

* WHEN...Until 300 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Barbourville, Cannon, Heidrick, Girdler, Baileys Switch, Hinkle,
Yeager, Jarvis, Bimble, Green Road, Boone Heights, Lowell,
Bentley Station, Emmanuel, Baughman, Garrich, Artemus, Dishman
Springs, Arkle and Barnyard.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 1:41AM EDT until September 23 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central Ohio, including the following
areas, Belmont, Monroe and Noble, Pennsylvania, including the
following areas, Allegheny, Fayette, Greene, Higher Elevations of
Fayette, Higher Elevations of Westmoreland, Washington and
Westmoreland, and West Virginia, including the following areas,
Brooke, Eastern Preston, Eastern Tucker, Marion, Marshall,
Monongalia, Ohio, Preston, Ridges of Eastern Monongalia and
Northwestern Preston, Western Tucker and Wetzel.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

rainfall are expected through Tuesday night. Additional rainfall
of 1 to 2 inches is expected on average, with locally higher
totals possible. Flash flooding is possible, particularly in
areas that have recently received heavy rain.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 1:25AM EDT until September 22 at 2:45AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
At 125 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 4.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Harlan, Loyall, Evarts, Kildav, Bailey Creek, Verda, Darkmont,
Putney, Ages, Short Town, Kenvir, Coxton, Colts, Black Mountain,
Nolansburg, Shields, Rosspoint, Golden Ash, Chevrolet and Lenarve.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

North Central Dickenson County in southwestern Virginia...

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain

shortly.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Grundy, Haysi, Breaks Interstate, John Flannagan Lake, Big Rock,
Roseann and Hurley.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Citrus and Marion
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall water levels remain elevated along the
Horse Creek near Arcadia, and is expected to drop below flood stage
overnight.

July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a

levels to rise.

impassable.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 21 at 6:07PM MDT until September 23 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All of south-central and southwestern New Mexico, as well
as El Paso and western Hudspeth Counties in Texas. The area of
greatest concern will be near and east of the Continental Divide to
the Tularosa Basin and Sacramento Mountains.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and
rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cool front will interact with a late
season plume of deep tropical moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Ohio, including the following county,
Washington and West Virginia, including the following counties,
Barbour, Boone, Braxton, Cabell, Calhoun, Clay, Doddridge, Gilmer,
Harrison, Jackson WV, Kanawha, Lewis, Lincoln, Logan, Mason,
McDowell, Mingo, Northwest Fayette, Northwest Nicholas, Northwest
Pocahontas, Northwest Raleigh, Northwest Randolph, Northwest
Webster, Pleasants, Putnam, Ritchie, Roane, Southeast Fayette,
Southeast Nicholas, Southeast Pocahontas, Southeast Raleigh,
Southeast Randolph, Southeast Webster, Taylor, Tyler, Upshur,
Wayne, Wirt, Wood and Wyoming.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Slow moving heavy showers and thunderstorms will periodically
move through the area through Tuesday night. Areas which have
previously received heavy rain will be most vulnerable to
additional flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 3:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the YK Delta. While the most likely storm
track south of our area would result in only modest rises in above
normal high water, a further north track could result in high
surf potential. As of right now, the southern portion of the YK
Delta coast could see water levels rise to around 1 to 3 feet
above the mean high water line. We will continue to monitor this
system closely.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF POTENTIAL FOR YUKON DELTA COAST TOWARD END OF THE WEEK

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT IN EFFECT

properties.areaDesc: Northwest Highlands; West Central Mountains; West Central Highlands; Southwest Mountains; Jemez Mountains; Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass; Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains; East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains; Espanola Valley; Santa Fe Metro Area; Middle Rio Grande Valley/Albuquerque Metro Area; Lower Rio Grande Valley; Sandia/Manzano Mountains Including Edgewood; Estancia Valley; Central Highlands; South Central Highlands; Upper Tularosa Valley; South Central Mountains; Far Northeast Highlands; Northeast Highlands; Harding County; Eastern San Miguel County; Guadalupe County; De Baca County; Chaves County Plains; Eastern Lincoln County; Southwest Chaves County; San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 21 at 2:23PM MDT until September 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the
following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern
Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle
Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin
Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains
including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central
Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De
Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East
Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa
Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands,
Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In
northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast
Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New
Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west
central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and
West Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount
by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along
and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many
locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms
will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour,
and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some
locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6
inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico.  Heavy
rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas,
then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast
to return along and east of the continental divide again on
Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.  Never drive through flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 21 at 3:27PM EDT until September 25 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet expected in the surf zone.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of inundation
above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Atlantic Coastal Cape May, Coastal Atlantic and
Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Tuesday morning
through Friday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from
4 PM to 10 PM EDT Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8
AM Wednesday to 6 PM EDT Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
from Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS....Significant beach erosion is likely
through this week and into the weekend. Moderate tidal flooding
could continue through Friday or perhaps longer.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

properties.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 21 at 2:43PM EDT until September 22 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Ohio...

Hocking River at Athens affecting Athens County.

For the Hocking River...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Hocking River at Athens.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Low areas, campground, and private camps
along the river between Athens and Coolville begin to flood. Much
of the city of Athens is protected up to 26 feet by levees. In
Nelsonville, the baseball field adjacent to Lake Hope Drive floods.
At 21.0 feet, South Canaan Road and Township Road 605 in the
vicinity of US Route 50 flood. Glen Ebon Road begins to flood.
Hockhocking Adena Bikeway near West State Street begins to flood.
In Chauncey, areas along Ohio Routes 13 and 682 flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EDT Monday the stage was 20.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 PM EDT Monday was 20.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.0 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.8
feet on 04/06/2025.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rlx.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 245 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 7:14PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
CORRECTED HEADLINE.

...HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE AND PALAU
THROUGH MIDWEEK...
...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES...

An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that
is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to
organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at
times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day

properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that
is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to
organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at
times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day
through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the
